_about: Programmes written by hand that are not in the programme bank (tools/bank.json is regenerated by import_bank.py, so they live here). Same fields as bank.json, plus 'when' and 'practical', which replace or add rows in the practical details. Facts checked on 15 Oct 2026: the National Museum on Janpath is open Tuesday to Sunday and closed on Mondays (Time Out Delhi, Sep 2026); the Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays (tajmahal.gov.in); most of the Chandni Chowk main market is shut on Sundays.

programmes.title: The National Museum, New Delhi, with an archaeologist
programmes.subtitle: A guided visit to India's National Museum on Janpath, from the Harappan gallery to Mughal painting
programmes.description: The National Museum on Janpath holds one of the largest collections in India: Harappan seals and the bronze 'dancing girl', early historic and Buddhist sculpture, bronzes from south India and Mughal and Rajput paintings. An archaeologist takes your group through the galleries that matter most for your interests and shows you how to read an object: what it is made of, where it was found, and what it can and cannot tell us.
programmes.for: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
programmes.takeaway: A one-page trail of the objects you saw, with a reading list
highlights: The Harappan gallery: seals, weights, pottery and the bronze 'dancing girl'
Early historic and Buddhist sculpture, including the art of Gandhara

plan.title: Orientation
plan.detail: How the museum is arranged, and the galleries chosen for your group.

plan.title: The Harappan gallery
plan.detail: Seals, weights, ornaments and pottery from the Harappan cities, and what they show about trade, crafts and writing.
plan.activity: Read a seal and a weight: what was each one for?

plan.title: Sculpture
plan.detail: Early historic and Buddhist sculpture, and how styles changed from region to region.
plan.activity: Compare two Buddha images and date them from their details

plan.title: Bronzes
plan.detail: Bronze images from south India and how they were cast and carried in procession.

plan.title: Paintings
plan.detail: Mughal and Rajput painting: who commissioned a painting, and what it was for.
plan.activity: Find the patron and the story in one painting

plan.title: Wrap-up
plan.detail: Your questions, and what to see on a second visit.

objectives: Read a museum object for its material, findspot, date and purpose.
Follow India's past from the Harappan cities to the Mughal court through the National Museum's collection.
Tell what an object shows from what a label or a later story adds to it.
programmes.when: Tuesday to Sunday. The National Museum is closed on Mondays.

practical.Meeting point: The main entrance of the National Museum on Janpath.
practical.Entry fees: The museum's entry fee is not included.

programmes.title: Old Delhi: a Chandni Chowk heritage walk
programmes.subtitle: A walk along Shahjahanabad's main street and its bazaars, from the Red Fort end to Fatehpuri Masjid
programmes.description: Chandni Chowk was laid out around 1650 as the main street of Shahjahanabad, the city Shah Jahan built beside the Red Fort. Walk it with a historian or archaeologist from the Red Fort end to Fatehpuri Masjid and read the street as a document: places of worship of several faiths along one road, bazaars that still keep their trades, and the havelis, katras and lanes behind the frontage.
programmes.for: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
programmes.led_by: A historian or archaeologist who specialises in Delhi's buildings
programmes.takeaway: A street map of the buildings you saw, with their dates
highlights: One street, several faiths: the Digambar Jain Lal Mandir, the Gauri Shankar temple, Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib and the Sunehri Masjid
Dariba Kalan, Kinari Bazaar and the spice market of Khari Baoli
Havelis and katras behind the main street
Fatehpuri Masjid at the western end of the street

plan.title: The Red Fort end
plan.detail: How Shahjahanabad was planned around the fort and its main street.

plan.title: One street, several faiths
plan.detail: The Lal Mandir, the Gauri Shankar temple, Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib and the Sunehri Masjid, visited respectfully and only where visitors are welcome.
plan.activity: Date each building from its details

plan.title: The bazaars
plan.detail: Dariba Kalan, Kinari Bazaar and Khari Baoli: how a trade keeps its lane for generations.

plan.title: Havelis and katras
plan.detail: The houses and courtyard markets behind the main street, and what has happened to them.

plan.title: Fatehpuri Masjid
plan.detail: The mosque that closes the street at its western end.

plan.title: Wrap-up
plan.detail: Your questions, and where to eat or shop before you leave.

objectives: Read Chandni Chowk as the planned main street of Shahjahanabad.
Recognise how places of worship, bazaars and houses shared one street.
Distinguish the Mughal-period fabric from later rebuilding along the street.
programmes.when: Monday to Saturday, when the bazaars are open; most shops in the main market are shut on Sundays. Mornings are best.

practical.Meeting point: Agreed with you, near Chandni Chowk metro station or the Red Fort end of the street.
practical.What to bring: Comfortable shoes and a small bag worn in front. The lanes are narrow and crowded. Shoes come off and heads are covered where a place of worship asks.
practical.Entry fees: None of the places on the walk charges an entry fee.

programmes.title: Agra in a day: the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort
programmes.subtitle: A day trip from Delhi by car, with an archaeologist at both World Heritage Sites
programmes.description: Agra was a Mughal capital under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan. This day trip by car from Delhi takes you to its two World Heritage Sites with an archaeologist: the Taj Mahal, read as a garden tomb and as a feat of planning and building, and Agra Fort, from Akbar's red sandstone walls to Shah Jahan's marble palaces. The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah or the Mehtab Bagh garden across the river can be added if time allows.
programmes.for: Schools, colleges, companies and the public
programmes.length: A full day of about 12 hours, with 3 to 4 hours' drive each way
programmes.led_by: An archaeologist or historian of Mughal architecture
programmes.takeaway: A plan of the Taj Mahal garden and Agra Fort, marked with what you saw
highlights: The Taj Mahal: the garden, the gateway, the tomb and the riverfront
How the Taj Mahal was planned and built, and what is still debated
Agra Fort: Akbar's red sandstone and Shah Jahan's marble palaces
The view of the Taj Mahal from the fort

plan.title: Early start from Delhi
plan.detail: By car on the Yamuna Expressway, with a briefing on the Mughal capitals on the way.

plan.title: The Taj Mahal
plan.detail: The gateway, the garden, the tomb and the riverfront, read against the written sources and the building itself.
plan.activity: Mark the garden's plan and its axes

plan.title: Lunch
plan.detail: At a restaurant in Agra, or a place of your choice.

plan.title: Agra Fort
plan.detail: Akbar's red sandstone fort and the marble palaces added by Shah Jahan, ending with the view of the Taj Mahal from the fort.
plan.activity: Tell Akbar's buildings from Shah Jahan's

plan.title: Optional stop
plan.detail: The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah or the Mehtab Bagh garden, if time and light allow.

plan.detail: Your questions on the drive back.

objectives: Read the Taj Mahal as a planned garden tomb, not only a single building.
Distinguish the work of Akbar and of Shah Jahan at Agra Fort.
Separate what the sources say about the Taj Mahal from popular stories about it.
programmes.when: Any day except Friday, when the Taj Mahal is closed. October to March is the most comfortable season, and an early start means a quieter Taj Mahal.

practical.Travel: The car from Delhi and back is included in the price.
practical.Meals: Not included. Lunch is at a restaurant in Agra or a place of your choice.
practical.Entry fees: Monument entry fees are not included. The Taj Mahal's main tomb has its own ticket on top of the entry ticket.
